title: Explicit bounds for the zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions
summary: The numerically explicit layer above ZerosOfLFunctions: the O* error calculus; bounded-height RH(H) and GRH(q, H) with the bridge from Platt's finite-conductor theorem; Stirling's series with Stieltjes', Lindelöf's, Brent's and Nemes' remainder bounds, Binet's formulas, the two-sided modulus bound for Γ and real-axis Gamma, digamma and polygamma brackets; the explicit Phragmén–Lindelöf principle and Rademacher's convexity bound on records of finite-order type; Backlund's strip bounds, bounds right of one and explicit approximate functional equations; the explicit van der Corput toolkit (Kusmin–Landau, A- and B-processes, derivative tests), the explicit Vinogradov mean value theorem with Richert-type bounds, the Riemann–Siegel formula with Gabcke's remainder and the critical-line, one-line and σ_k-line bounds; Backlund's argument lemma and the explicit Riemann–von Mangoldt formulas for ζ and L(s, χ); weighted zero sums; smoothed and averaged Perron formulas, the majorant principle, Preissmann's weighted Hilbert inequality, mean values and weighted and maximal large sieves; classical, Littlewood-type and Vinogradov–Korobov zero-free regions with decimal constants, Dirichlet regions, real-zero bounds and the capped real-zero gap with its numerical instances; zero-density estimates; and upper and lower bounds for L(1, χ). Computations enter only as named certificates; the explicit Vinogradov mean value theorem and the exponential-sum bound behind the Vinogradov–Korobov targets are stated here (4.9a).
